To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of cache memory systems for vector processors can be predicted analytically by analyzing the algorithm structure and the system architecture.

the cache performance of vector computers can be predicted by analytical models that are based on real applications and that the prime-mapping cache is the best choice to minimize the miss ratio of numerical applications.

(a) the performance of a cache is highly sensitive to its mapping scheme; (b) the performance of blocked numerical algorithms can be accurately predicted by our analytical models; and (c) a prime-mapped cache can improve the performance of blocked algorithms by 2 to 4 times over a direct-mapped cache.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of cache memories for vector computers.
performance modeling of numerical applications on vector computers.
a fundamental problem of designing high performance computers: how to reduce the memory latency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prime-mapping cache is a good choice for vector processors.
the prime-mapping technique is superior in terms of performance and cost to the direct-mapping technique.
the prime-mapping cache is a good choice to be incorporated into vector computers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cache performance depends on both algorithm structures and cache organizations.

the performance of the prime-mapped caches is comparable to that of the direct-mapped caches for the algorithms studied, and the prime-mapped organization can be used as an alternative to the direct-mapped organization.
the prime-mapping cache organization is superior to the direct-mapping cache in terms of performance, and it can be implemented efficiently on vector computers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cache memories can improve the performance of vector computers by an order of magnitude.
the performance of vector computers can be improved significantly by incorporating cache memories.
cache performance can be predicted accurately by analyzing algorithm structures in conjunctions with system architectures.
